# Switch — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a switch when flipping it takes effect immediately and does not need a save step: notifications on, dark mode, auto-play. It is a thin wrapper over one Base UI primitive — the whole component is a stateful root and a thumb, and kern supplies the M3 look and the focus ring rather than any behaviour of its own. If the change only applies after a tap on a separate save button, that is a checkbox, not a switch. A switch carries its state in its own appearance, so it needs a visible label next to it rather than a label that only exists for assistive tech.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use for a single on/off that applies immediately — Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, notifications.
- Label every switch — visible text or `aria-label`.
- Use icons to emphasize the selected state where the meaning benefits.

**Don't**

- Don't use for multi-choices — that is a checkbox.
- Don't use for one-of-many — that is a radio group.
- Don't render without a name — an unnamed switch cannot be announced.

| Selected track | disabled | comp.switch.disabled-track-opacity | on-surface 12% |

### FAQ

**Switch or checkbox?**

Switch for a single on/off that applies immediately. Checkbox for independent choices, possibly several at once.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a switch when flipping it takes effect straight away and there is no save step: notifications on, dark mode, auto-play. It is a pressable with `checked`/`onCheckedChange`, and the state is visible in the control itself, so it needs a label beside it that says WHAT is on. Note there is no `label` prop here at all — unlike `Checkbox`, which offers one and warns about omitting it. Naming the switch is entirely yours, usually with a `Label` or text beside it. If the change only applies after tapping a separate save button, that is a checkbox, not a switch.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use for settings that take effect the moment they flip — the switch IS the commit.
- Keep one switch per row with its label beside it, so the announcement names what flips.
- Drive `checked` from state when the setting can change from elsewhere (server push, reset-all).

**Don't**

- Don't use a switch for form options that submit together — those are checkboxes.
- Don't hide the state in color alone — the thumb's side and the track fill carry it together.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Track on | checked | theme.color.primary | primary track, 52×32 |
| Track off | resting | theme.color.outline | 2px outline border on surface |
| Thumb on | checked | theme.color.onPrimary | onPrimary 24px thumb, trailing side |
| Thumb off | resting | theme.color.outline | outline 16px thumb, leading side |
| Track shape | resting | theme.shape.full | full pill, pressed dims to 0.82 |

### FAQ

**Switch or checkbox?**

Immediate effect means switch; submit-together options mean checkbox. If flipping it does nothing until save, it is not a switch.

**How does this differ from the web switch?**

Same `checked` vocabulary, same 52×32 geometry. The track and thumb are kern-drawn styles (with `switch-track-shape` theming the container) rather than Base UI parts, and state is `accessibilityState`, not ARIA.
